parsed.explanation: The operative regime has strong paper protections: constitutional and statutory gender-identity non-discrimination, a Penal Code discrimination offence, and a hate-crime aggravator. Same-sex conduct is lawful and no trans-specific border, facility, custody or care ban is documented. The main deduction is weak enforcement and documented societal discrimination: the 2017 ombudsman found most LGBT murders uninvestigated and none sentenced, and a 2024 survey recorded widespread LGBTI exclusion. No visitor-targeted violence or state threat-framing is documented. Border, facility and minor-specific practice remain uncertain. This places the jurisdiction below well-enforced protection regimes but well above jurisdictions with traveller-facing denial, detention, or criminalisation.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented border screening, marker-mismatch refusal, or denial rule aimed at trans visitors.
entry_documents.protection: Constitutional and statutory gender-identity protections; foreign documents are not documented as rejected.
entry_documents.interaction: Passport checks remain an ordinary outing point, but no systematic referral or refusal practice is documented.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Enforcement against anti-LGBT violence is weak: 2017 ombudsman reporting found most recorded murders uninvestigated and none sentenced.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Penal Code art. 281 and art. 40bis provide discrimination offences and sentencing aggravation.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Weak investigation may leave trans victims without effective recourse, but no trans-specific detention or custody exposure is documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No bathroom, ward, shelter, or single-sex facility restriction is documented for visitors.
federal_state_facilities.protection: The 2010 anti-discrimination law covers services, health, education, and public and private spheres.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facilities operate under national law, and no subnational variation is documented.

care_services.exposure: No documented denial of transition-related or emergency care to visitors; broad LGBTI exclusion is recorded but not care-specific.
care_services.protection: Anti-discrimination law covers health services, and no trans-specific care ban is documented.
care_services.interaction: Resident gender-recognition procedures do not govern visitors; ordinary visitor care access is untested in the dossier.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No state threat-framing, cross-dressing law, or impersonation offence targeting trans visitors is documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Constitution, Penal Code art. 281, and art. 40bis aggravator protect gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Law is protective on paper, but enforcement is documented as weak; no official hostile campaign is documented.

minors_guardians.exposure: No minor-specific restriction is documented; treatment of a trans minor with a guardian at borders or facilities is unknown.
minors_guardians.protection: Anti-discrimination law covers education and services; adoption and free-union rules are resident-facing only.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family would mainly face ordinary ID and facility checks; no age-dependent hostile rule is documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Societal discrimination is reported as common, and a 2017 report says LGBT murders were rarely investigated or sentenced.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime aggravation, anti-discrimination law, and majority poll support for trans rights are documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police and courts are weak on anti-LGBT violence, but no visitor-targeted pattern or organised targeting is documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Enforcement gaps persist; official investigation figures are limited to 2017, and recent outcomes are not documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Ombudsman, courts, and statutory complaint routes exist; a regional human-rights appeal was lodged.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Paper remedies are not shown to operate consistently for trans people, and no visitor-specific remedy data is documented.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A has a routine border register denying entry to trans visitors. This dossier documents no traveller-facing entry ban or routine exclusion, so it sits materially higher.

0.55-B documents extended secondary screening and discretionary refusal at borders. Here border friction is not documented; the deduction comes from weak enforcement and social discrimination, not state exclusion, so this rating is higher.

0.65-A has a concrete mismatch stop with intrusive questioning but a working remedy and reliable release. This dossier has broader statutory protection but weaker documented enforcement and no comparable remedy evidence, so it is broadly similar or slightly higher.

0.75-C documents trained border officers and a functioning tribunal, with low severity. This dossier has stronger anti-discrimination statutes on paper but weaker documented enforcement, so it sits somewhat below 0.75-C.

parsed.synthesis: The combined national regime is legally protective but operationally uneven. A trans visitor faces no documented criminalisation, entry ban, facility exclusion, or trans-specific custody rule; the strongest documented negatives are weak investigation of anti-LGBT violence and common societal discrimination. That produces real but non-catastrophic exposure if outed. Because no subnational regime varies the rules, the rating applies nationwide. Open questions at borders, in facilities, and for minors with guardians keep it below well-enforced protection anchors, while the absence of traveller-facing state exclusion keeps it well above denial-and-detention regimes.
